newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks likely to rise, yen/dlr to be watched.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks likely to rise, yen/dlr to be watched.

text.p: Seoul stocks are expected to rise on Tuesday on hopes for benefits from falling interest rates and the new strength of the Japanese yen, brokers said.
On Monday the composite index soared 1.6 percent, or 12.24 points, to 775.01, the highest closing since October 28, 1996.
"Securities firms are likely to lead the rally as investors believed brokerages would benefit most from the low interest rates," said Lee Kye-joon of Daishin Securities.
Almost all listed securities firms rose by their daily limits of eight percent on Monday, with the sector's sub-index rising 7.64 percent, or 104.85 points, to 1,476.52.

Many investors bet that the yen's strength could help South Korean exports to come out of a long slump. Economists say a stronger yen would generally make South Korean products more price competitive in export markets against Japanese goods.
The yen once rose to 111.80 against the dollar on Monday in Tokyo, the highest since November 25, 1996.
Recent drops in local interest rates are also underlining the rally. On Monday, the benchmark three-year corporate bonds closed at 11.38 percent, the lowest since June 11, 1996.
